claim_en: THE PLEA: I BESOUGHT THE LORD AT THAT TIME — O LORD GOD, YOU HAVE BEGUN TO SHOW YOUR SERVANT YOUR GREATNESS AND YOUR STRONG HAND; WHAT GOD IN HEAVEN OR EARTH CAN DO ACCORDING TO YOUR WORKS? LET ME CROSS OVER, I PRAY, AND SEE THE GOOD LAND BEYOND THE JORDAN, THAT GOOD HILL COUNTRY AND LEBANON. 'And I besought' a hapax form (the grace-root's hitpael; Onkelos 'I prayed before the LORD'); 'O LORD GOD' the Torah's four seats — Abraham's two (Genesis 15:2, 8) and Moses' two; 'your greatness' 3:24 and Joshua 3:7; 'your strong hand' 3:24 and Solomon's prayer (1 Kings 8:42); 'according to your works and your mighty acts' a hapax pair; ONKELOS TURNS THE QUESTION INTO A CONFESSION — 'God whose Shekhinah is in the heavens above and who rules on the earth'; 'let me cross over, I pray' three seats (Jephthah's embassy, Abishai's); 'that good hill' one seat; Lebanon plene as at 1:7 — Onkelos 'THE HOUSE OF THE SANCTUARY' here (three seats in the book), the Sifrei 6:2 and 28:3's reading written. The Sifrei 26: the poor man's supplication (Proverbs 18:23); Moses and David the two providers, the sin recorded, the three Meribahs, a free gift asked; THE TEN NAMES OF PRAYER, this the tenth; 'at that time' after Sihon and Og fell; 'saying' — tell me whether; the two names mercy and judgment. 27 (no head citation, continuing 3:24): 'you have begun' — the vow to Jethro released, the door opened at the calf (the many's prayer for one a fortiori); the servants; 'your greatness' THE BINYAN AV named; the strong hand the ten plagues; no deputy to fear; works in Egypt, might at the sea (or the Jordan). 28: the servant who loves the decree; the mountain everyone named; Lebanon the sanctuary that whitens sins.
middah: ink (the hapax forms, the names' four seats, the prayer's and the hill's seats censused; the translation's confession measured against the question); I3 (27:4 — the Sifrei names the binyan av on 'your greatness'); I1 (26:6, 27:2); I5 (26:9 — the superfluous 'saying'); E7 (27:5 — the strong hand from Exodus 8:1; 28:3 — Lebanon from Jeremiah 22:6)

claim_en: THE REFUSAL AND THE CHARGE: THE LORD WAS WROTH WITH ME FOR YOUR SAKES AND WOULD NOT HEAR — ENOUGH FOR YOU, SPEAK NO MORE OF THIS; GO UP TO THE TOP OF PISGAH, LIFT UP YOUR EYES WEST, NORTH, SOUTH AND EAST AND SEE WITH YOUR EYES, FOR YOU SHALL NOT CROSS THIS JORDAN; CHARGE JOSHUA, STRENGTHEN AND ENCOURAGE HIM, FOR HE SHALL CROSS BEFORE THIS PEOPLE AND CAUSE THEM TO INHERIT THE LAND; AND WE DWELT IN THE VALLEY OPPOSITE BETH-PEOR. 'Was wroth' the hitpael's nine tokens (Psalm 78's three), the store glossing the pass-root's homograph beside 'let me cross'; 'for your sakes' four seats (1:37's and 4:21's the other tellings); 'ENOUGH FOR YOU' the singular's one seat — the plural's eight (Korah's first) turned on Moses; Onkelos 'did not accept from me' — the words it gave 1:45's people; 'go up to the top of Pisgah' — Numbers 27:12's Abarim, 32:49's Nebo, 34:1's 'Nebo, the top of Pisgah' (the outside row 37:11's three names); 'LIFT UP YOUR EYES WEST, NORTH, SOUTH, EAST' — Genesis 13:14's charge to Abram with the directions in ANOTHER ORDER, Genesis 28:14's a third; 'and see with your eyes' 3:27 and Ezekiel 44:5; 'you shall not cross this Jordan' one seat (31:2 quotes it); 'strengthen him and encourage him' one seat, 'be strong and of good courage' nine; 'he shall cause them to inherit' one seat — Numbers 27:19-23's commissioning told as the charge, Joshua 1:6 the run; 'opposite Beth-peor' three seats — 4:46's place-stamp and 34:6 MOSES' GRAVE. The Sifrei 29: wroth — filled with wrath (R. Eliezer) or as a woman with child (R. Joshua); 'for your sakes'; 'did not accept my prayer'; 'ENOUGH' — go to your master to release your vow; the judges' example and prayer never withheld (Hezekiah's sword); much kept for you; a prayer worth a hundred deeds — 'go up'; THE DIRECTIONS OF PRAYER, all Israel toward one place; the son at the bedroom door — a rope of fifty cubits refused; charging is urging (31:7 — Torah and deeds); if he crosses they cross, if he gives they inherit — AI'S THIRTY-SIX the breach. 30: what made us dwell in the valley — Peor; the difference between you and me; the right hand receives the penitent — 'and now, Israel' (4:1).
middah: ink (the wrath-verb's, the singular 'enough', the directions' three orders, the Pisgah names' and the grave's seats censused; the translation's one phrase at 1:45 and 3:26 measured); I1 (29:3 — the judges, Hezekiah); E7 (29:7 — 'charge' from 31:7); LR1 (29:9 — Joshua 7 read as the breach of 3:28's rule, taught by the Sifrei); the shelf's own measure flagged (29:6 — fifty cubits, not the ink's)
